catalog_rows.claim: The funding output is P2WSH over the constructed 2-of-2 funding witness script; the handshake construction derives the witness-script hash link, the vendored interpreter executes the funding script, and the BIP 143 witness-v0 digest/locktime context is constructed and consumed by the vendor checker under explicit signature laws; the joint open/accept construction proves the same hash link. The concrete ECDSA seam is characterized: the pointwise `VendorEcdsaBridge` with C3 forces total rejection, and no fixed tag satisfies `DigestBindsMod`; the exact repair is a canonical fixed-size value-`< n` domain, but the 33-byte instance is an abstract canonical 33-byte payload, not the real `fundingTag ++ tx` byte string, and the 32-byte instance is a digest-sized interface. Both are conditional and do not close the real funding-signature seam; a typed-digest model change or a concrete secp256k1 verifier is still required.

An anchor output is worth exactly 330 satoshis.

catalog_rows.claim: Constructed and opened payment hashes are SHA-256 outputs; under assumption C1 (collision resistance on the 32-byte preimage domain), a payment hash determines at most one valid preimage.
Under assumption C3 (ECDSA EUF-CMA), a commitment-domain signature binds its untagged message uniquely and cannot verify in the funding or close signing domain.
Onion HMAC-SHA256 tags are 32 bytes; under the finite-execution C8 admission, an authentic tag determines the hop payloads uniquely among the messages of that execution.
BigSize encoding and decoding are inverse on canonical encodings.
A TLV stream is well formed exactly when its types are pairwise strictly increasing, and well-formed streams have no duplicate record types.
A Lightning message frame's declared length matches the payload actually consumed.
Every ledger transition preserves funding = local + remote + in-flight + fee.
No commitment output has a negative value and the output sum stays within the funding value.

In the rich commitment-output model, outputs are sorted by value, script, and CLTV, and dust HTLCs are trimmed; the five-field gross/net record layer proves the canonical commitment refinement, migration conservation, and effective fee at arbitrary dust, while the legacy output function remains refuted by D12; the consumer migration preserves the legacy list only in the BOLT 3 survivor normal form, and the no-trim counterexample is retained.
A committed update never decreases the commitment number.
A commitment is rejected before signing exactly when its feerate is insufficient for its weight, equivalently when no checked commitment_signed step exists in the normal phase.
HTLC exposure and channel reserve bounds are respected by admissible updates.

catalog_rows.claim: Aggregate multi-HTLC second-stage coverage is the row-wise coverage of the full aggregate under explicit no-duplication and distinct-commitment hypotheses; one second-stage spend cannot cover two rows without an aliasing collision, aggregate weight/fee accounting is exact, and the legacy commitment_signed wire does not carry aggregate coverage.
A fulfilled HTLC carries a preimage whose hash is the payment hash.
An HTLC is failed only at or after its CLTV expiry.
Offered, received, and trimmed HTLC amounts plus balances and fee equal the funding value.
An HTLC id is unique among the live HTLCs of one sender; a direction-tagged id is globally unique, while the untagged global claim needs explicit cross-direction disjointness.
A revoked commitment is strictly older than the current commitment and cannot be the current one.
A punishable breach has a penalty transaction that spends both commitment outputs.

open_channel accepts a funding amount only above the dust and minimum-channel bounds. The routed envelope is attributed only by transport-key equality; the wire payload alone does not determine its sender, carries no signature, and the concrete route reaches `funding_created` under explicit transport/C1 hypotheses. A transport-authentication interface separates an authenticated session from the explicit `SessionKeyBinding` law; attributed delivery composes with the routed funding witness, while the same wire can be attributed under one session key and not another and no payload-only sender function exists. Model boundary: `TransportAuthenticated` is a session flag and `SessionKeyBinding` is the explicit equality `peerKey = fundingPubKey`; this is not a real Noise_XK/AEAD or EUF-CMA authentication claim.
The channel enters normal operation only after both channel_ready messages.

Under an explicit signing law and key-binding hypothesis, funding_signed carries a valid signature over the funding transaction and attributes it to the funding key; one joint contract also covers commitment_signed, while C3 alone gives neither; a secret-key model proves attribution under the unchanged KeyBinding and mechanizes why key generation alone does not attribute. A registration/proof-of-possession game over `StoredAccept` proves conditional attribution, shows storage is not possession, and retains the dropped-`KeyBinding` counterexample. A concrete challenge-response PoP protocol signs `popTag ++ channelId ++ nonce`; fixed-width validity makes the encoding injective, the session-bound verifier recomputes it from the verifier's challenge, and honest completeness, wave-9 `StoredRegistration` composition, and conditional funding attribution are proved. `PopKeySoundOn` is the weakest law used; unbound-challenge, nonce-free, no-`Valid`, and reused-challenge replay are mechanised counterexamples, with `EufCma` plus freshness identified as the preventing hypotheses. No real signature scheme or computational EUF-CMA claim is made.

Under a BOLT 3-shaped serializer with an exact transaction wire layout, an explicit signing law, and the commitment value equations, commitment_signed covers exactly the current HTLC set and fee and its digest/signatures are derived under C3; digest binding implies view binding only under explicit collision-free/serialization hypotheses, and the wire record alone determines neither; the commitment-wire preimage is byte-equal to the vendored BIP 143 encoder, with the HTLC instantiation still open. The eight arbitrary-preimage field hypotheses are explicit and complete; conditional byte/digest/signature transfer is mechanized, dropped-locktime/amount counterexamples are retained, and wire-only legacy coverage remains negative. The missing legacy-wire data is characterized as a per-HTLC coverage witness: the canonical witness decodes exactly to the full record's coverage, no legacy-only decoder or wire-compatible witness selector is correct for all full records, the amount row is necessary, and the same legacy message admits distinct decoding witnesses. A production decoder therefore requires an out-of-band/full-record source or a protocol change. A consumer contract composes with those sources: a full-record source yields an exact consumer unconditionally, no wire-determined consumer exists, and an extension determines one only under the explicit `ExtensionConsumerLaw`; concrete witnesses exercise all three source constructors.

A newer channel_update replaces an older one only if its timestamp is greater. Node announcements gain an additive canonical layer with strict-timestamp replacement, rotation/equal-timestamp boundaries, and epoch-square preservation. Node announcements gain an additive identity/linkage layer: canonically distinct wire `nodeId`s are not linked by any antisymmetric store-only relation, an explicit `RotationWitness` preserves wire membership without preserving signatures, and wire membership requires both `channel_announcement` wire keys to have node announcements but is not enforced by the core transition. Address parsing/canonicality is now modelled separately (BOLT 7 `u16 addrlen` blob and typed descriptors); identity across rotation, chain-existence policy, and a production gossip/rotation pipeline remain open. The epoch-square lift is conditional on the raw fold's `Nodup`/`CanonicalNodeAnnouncements` invariant.
